narr: Tropical Storm Hilary made landfall across northern Baja California on August 20, and moved through Southern California that afternoon and evening. Torrential rainfall occurred across mountain and desert communities, resulting in catastrophic flash flooding and debris flows, damaged railways and bridges, and the closing of major interstates including I-8 in San Diego County and I-10 in Riverside County. Widespread tropical-storm force winds were recorded across much of Southern California.
ev: A swift water rescue was conducted on Box Canyon Road in Mecca.
Multiple reports of roadway flooding on I-10 in Cabazon.
Two vehicles were stuck in rushing water on Dillon Road and Landfill Road.
Video received from this area near Sheep Creek showing boulders, rocks, and high water over State Highway 2 after 6.23 inches of rain fell. Time is estimated.

Video received from Potato Canyon in Oak Glen of mud and rocks across the roadway. Mud and rocks surround a residence in Oak Glen following a debris flow. Widespread rocks and mud covers many roadways in the town.
Portions of State Highway 38 near the Heart Bar Campground were washed out.

Thirty residents in Seven Oaks were cut off from rescue after the Santa Ana River overflowed and Glass Road was damaged. One person was missing at the time of report, potentially washed into Barton Creek. Seven Oaks Road was closed for Emergency Crews.
Highway 78 was washed out at Yaqui Pass.

Union Pacific rail tracks were undercut and washed out when the Whitewater River broke a division bern at the California and Colorado River Aqueduct. At least one train was confirmed to have derailed, with two other trains either observed off track after being forced off the rails by floodwaters, or buried on track. Water and debris was estimated to be 10-15 feet high, and also buckled/cracked the bridge footing at Whitewater. This also severed fiber cables in the area, leading to outages.
A roughly 30-mile stretch of I-10 between Bob Hope Drive and Indian Canyon Drive was closed due to inundation by mud, debris, and flooding. Flooding covered Gene Autry Road in Palm Springs.
The Mias Canyon Bridge near the Apple Burn Scar was washed out due to heavy rain and flowing debris.
